strings.name: Ma Long
strings.summary: Born in Anshan, Ma joined China’s national team as a teenager and became a central player through all-round technique and consistency. He won world singles titles in 2015, 2017 and 2019, Olympic singles gold in 2016 and 2021, and Paris team gold in 2024, taking his Olympic tally to six golds. In 2025 he joined CTTA leadership.
strings.influence.rationale: Olympic and world champion whose sustained elite performance represents modern table tennis standards.
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied human resource management at Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s Antai College.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Six Olympic golds
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won two singles and four team golds from 2012 through 2024.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Three consecutive world singles titles
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won men’s singles in 2015, 2017 and 2019 consecutively.
strings.timeline.t1.title: CTTA vice-president
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined the vice-presidents in a CTTA leadership reshuffle.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Paris team gold
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won team gold with China, bringing his Olympic gold total to six.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Defended Olympic singles
strings.timeline.t3.text: Beat Fan Zhendong in Tokyo, becoming the first to defend Olympic men’s singles gold.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Third world singles title
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won singles in Budapest, completing three consecutive world titles.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Rio singles gold
strings.timeline.t5.text: Beat Zhang Jike to complete the Olympic, world championship and World Cup singles Grand Slam.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First world singles title
strings.timeline.t6.text: Beat Fang Bo in Suzhou for his first world singles championship.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined national team
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined China’s national team, developing through elite training and competition.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Anshan
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Anshan, Liaoning, and began table tennis in childhood.
